headline: AstraZeneca agreed a deal worth up to $1.5 billion with AI drug discovery company insitro to find treatments for a fatty liver disease and heart muscle diseases.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large headline figure for AI drug discovery, though only $40 million is paid upfront.
importance_line: Could speed the search for treatments for liver and heart muscle disease that affect many patients, but nearly all of the $1.5 billion is paid only if milestones are met, and no drug exists yet.
summary: BioSpace reports that insitro will receive $40 million upfront and could earn $1.46 billion more in milestone payments plus royalties, according to the company's 15 Oct 2026 announcement. The two will use insitro's Virtual Human AI platform to look for drug targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH, a fatty liver disease) and cardiomyopathies (heart muscle diseases), with AstraZeneca taking any candidates into development.
notes: WSJ original blocked; credited to BioSpace, which read the company announcement. Suggested category could be HEA; kept MKT as a deal story per chunk default.
